Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with ongoing right knee
pain, swelling, and reduced range of motion. Over the course of 28 visits, care
consisted of physical examination, imaging review, a structured physical therapy
program, and home exercise instruction. The reported knee complaints are consistent
with the mechanism and force of the collision as described in the history. Early visits
were frequent, and the treatment intensity tapered steadily as symptoms improved and
function returned. Some examination findings, including joint line tenderness and a
positive effusion sign, support the presence of a knee injury. Other tests, including
ligament stability assessments and neurovascular checks, were within normal limits. No
prior injury or treatment involving this body area is known from the patient's history
or records. Billed services reflect the care delivered, with no duplicated or repeated
charges identified. The patient is currently improving and is expected to continue a
home program with periodic follow-up as needed.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
